rules.effective_date_basis: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
rules.title: Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources required when ending a tenancy
rules.requirement: When a Boston landlord serves a Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal or expiration, the landlord must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time. Landlords and foreclosing owners must also send required notices and a certificate of compliance/service to Boston’s Office of Housing Stability.
rules.key_value: Notice required at the same time as Notice to Quit; 2nd and subsequent offenses: $300 per day

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when a landlord or foreclosing owner intends to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
coverage.summary: The ordinance applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy in Boston, except specified hospital, health-facility, and certain nonprofit treatment-facility residences.

rules.exemptions: The only exempt properties are residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.penalty: Violations are enforced by the Inspectional Services Department: 1st offense warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. The FAQ states that a violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.interaction: The document does not state any interaction with other state or local eviction rules; it states that failure to provide the notice does not halt the eviction process.
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
